sections.heading: C2 — More warning signs, crossing and construction signs, and confusables
sections.markdown:
## C2 — More warning signs, crossing and construction signs, and confusables

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A48
A ROAD NARROWS sign means the road ahead is narrower than the one you are on, and a PAVEMENT NARROWS sign means the paved surface ahead is narrower. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A48
An island-ahead warning sign means you may pass the island on either side. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A48
A DIP sign warns of a dip in the road and tells you to slow down. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A48
A ONE LANE BRIDGE sign means the bridge ahead has no room for you to meet or pass another car or truck. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F40 | anchor: A48
STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs warn that a STOP sign or a YIELD sign is coming up. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F41 | anchor: A48
Other warning signs show a sharp left turn followed by a sharp right, or a road that ends ahead and turns both right and left. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F42 | anchor: A49
An advisory speed sign gives the top safe speed for taking the turn ahead. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F43 | anchor: A49
Arrow signs warn of a sharp turn or curve in the direction of the arrow and are normally set up in a series. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F44 | anchor: A49
A railroad-crossing-ahead warning sign means slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, since a train cannot stop quickly. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F45 | anchor: A49
A low-shoulder sign warns that the shoulder sits much lower than the road surface. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F46 | anchor: A49
Truck-crossing and fire-station signs tell you to watch for trucks or fire trucks pulling onto the road. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F47 | anchor: A49
A PAVEMENT ENDS sign warns that the surface ahead turns to gravel or dirt, and a DEAD END sign means the street has no outlet. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F48 | anchor: A49
Lane-ends signs warn that the number of lanes changes ahead, and the three signs come in a series as a repeated reminder to merge into the next lane. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F49 | anchor: A50
The NO PASSING ZONE warning sign stands on the left side of a two-lane road to warn where a no-passing zone begins. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F50 | anchor: A50
A low-clearance sign means vehicles or loads taller than the clearance shown cannot fit under the structure ahead. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F51 | anchor: A50
A two-way traffic sign means you are leaving a separated one-way roadway for a two-way road, and it also reminds drivers they are on a two-way road. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F52 | anchor: A50
At a merge sign, a driver joining from the right gives way to main-route traffic and uses the speed-change lane to blend in smoothly. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F53 | anchor: A50
Other warning signs announce a traffic signal ahead, a crossroad, a divided highway starting or ending, and a downhill grade. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-F54 | anchor: A51
Warning signs also flag slippery-when-wet pavement, a narrow bridge, cattle crossings and deer crossings. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F55 | anchor: A51
A pedestrian-crossing sign marks a spot where people on foot often cross, not always at an intersection, and you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk while watching both sides. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F56 | anchor: A51
A school-crossing sign means slow down and watch for children crossing, and a separate sign warns of a school bus stop ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F57 | anchor: A51
Bicycle, pedestrian and school crossing signs may appear in either their older or their current colors. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F58 | anchor: A52
One bicycle sign states that a 3 foot minimum clearance is required when passing a cyclist. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F59 | anchor: A52
Another sign tells drivers that a cyclist may use the full lane when the travel lane is narrow. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F60 | anchor: A52
Shared lane markings, called sharrows, tell road users that people on bicycles may be riding in the travel lane. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F61 | anchor: A52
A ROAD CONSTRUCTION sign means you are entering a work area, so watch for a flagman, one-way traffic, other signs or obstructions, go carefully and follow instructions. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F62 | anchor: A52
Work-zone signs also warn of a flagman ahead, workers in or near the road, and mowing equipment ahead. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F63 | anchor: A52
Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels may be used in work zones by day and night to steer drivers into certain lanes and show that part of the road ahead is closed. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A46
Ordinary warning signs are black on yellow, construction warning signs are black on orange, and fluorescent yellow is kept for pedestrian crossings and school zones. [A46]
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint sec08-F03; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F28, sec08-F29.
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A50
The no-passing warning sign belongs on the left side of a two-lane road, at the point where the zone begins, so look left for it. [A50]
Why it matters: group_hint no-passing-signs; prereq_hint sec08-F04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec08-F22, sec08-F49.
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A48
STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs only warn that a control is coming; the stop or yield itself happens at the STOP or YIELD sign further on. [A48]
Why it matters: group_hint sign-types; prereq_hint sec08-F04; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F40, sec08-F09.
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A48
ROAD NARROWS refers to the whole road getting narrower, PAVEMENT NARROWS to the paved surface, and ONE LANE BRIDGE to a bridge too narrow to meet or pass. [A48]
Why it matters: group_hint narrowing-signs; prereq_hint sec08-F30; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F36, sec08-F39.
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0048]
